stem.text: Sand is added to a pile at a rate of R(t) cubic feet per hour, where R is a positive function and t is measured in hours. Using correct units, interpret the meaning of \( \frac{1}{8}\int_{8}^{16} R(t)\,dt \) in the context of the problem.

answer_key.label: It is the average rate at which sand is added to the pile over the time interval from \( t = 8 \) to \( t = 16 \) hours, measured in cubic feet per hour.

worked_solution.text: R(t) is a rate measured in cubic feet per hour, so integrating it over time multiplies by hours and gives an amount in cubic feet.
worked_solution.rule_named: units of a definite integral of a rate

worked_solution.text: The limits run from \( t = 8 \) to \( t = 16 \) hours, so \( \int_{8}^{16} R(t)\,dt \) is the total volume of sand added to the pile from \( t = 8 \) to \( t = 16 \) hours.
worked_solution.rule_named: integral of a rate is the accumulated change

worked_solution.text: Dividing by the length of the interval, 8 hours, turns the amount into an average rate, so the expression is the average rate at which sand is added to the pile from \( t = 8 \) to \( t = 16 \) hours, in cubic feet per hour.
